title: Restaurant flyers for takeout menus and orders
seoTitle: Restaurant flyers for takeout menus and orders
description: Flyers still work for takeout, specials, and phone orders. See where to hand them out, what to print, and how to connect them to calls.
question: Do restaurant flyers still work for takeout orders and local marketing?
answer: Yes, restaurant flyers still work when they are simple, local, and tied to a clear action like calling for pickup or delivery. They are strongest for nearby homes, offices, apartments, and regulars who already know your food. A good flyer should show your menu basics, hours, phone number, and a reason to call now.
summary: You will know how to make restaurant flyers that bring in more takeout calls and local orders.
intro:
Yes, restaurant flyers still work for takeout menus and local specials. They work best when they are simple, neighborhood-focused, and easy to act on right away.

For independent spots, a flyer can do what a lot of ads do not: put your phone number in someone’s hand, on their fridge, or in the office break room. That is useful for pizza shops, delis, family restaurants, and takeout counters that want more direct orders.

sections.h2: Why do restaurant flyers still bring in calls?
sections.body:
Flyers work because they stay visible. A person may scroll past an ad in seconds, but a flyer on a fridge, counter, bulletin board, or office desk can sit there until hunger hits.

They are also easy to understand. A busy customer does not need a long pitch. They need a few clear things:
- What you sell
- Where you are
- Your hours
- Your phone number
- How to order pickup or delivery

Here is a simple line you can print near the phone number: "Call to order pickup or delivery from our live menu."

For local takeout, flyers are often best in places where your regular customers already go: apartment lobbies, laundromats, salons, shops, office buildings, and community boards. If your restaurant already gets calls for the same 10 to 20 popular items, a flyer can remind people to order those items again.

A helpful rule: the flyer should make sense in 5 seconds. If someone cannot tell what to do next, it is too crowded.

sections.h2: What should go on a takeout flyer?
sections.body:
Keep the flyer short. Put the most ordered items first, not your whole menu. If your menu is long, the flyer should act like a shortcut, not a full replacement.

A practical flyer layout:
1. Restaurant name and logo or simple name block
2. 3 to 8 best-selling items
3. Hours
4. Address or neighborhood
5. Phone number in large type
6. A short offer or reason to order

Example flyer copy:
- Large cheese pizza
- Chicken parm hero
- Greek salad
- Mozzarella sticks
- Pickup and delivery
- Open late Friday and Saturday
- Call to order from our live menu

If you use [pickup order taking](/use-cases/pickup-orders), the flyer can say that plainly. If you want to support questions about hours, address, parking, and the menu, add a line like: "Questions about the menu or hours? Call us."

A good flyer also avoids confusion. Do not list items you do not have. If something is sold out, remove it from the menu and from the flyer. ROAL reads the live menu, so the phone host does not offer items marked sold out. That helps keep the call consistent with what is actually available.

sections.h2: Where should I hand out flyers so they pay off?
sections.body:
Flyers work best when they go where your customers already live, work, or wait around hungry. Think local and repeatable, not random.

Good places to use them:
- Apartment buildings and lobbies where allowed
- Office break rooms
- Laundromats
- Barber shops and salons
- Community boards
- Nearby shops that let you leave a stack
- Counter bags for current customers to take home

Use a simple script when asking a nearby business: "We’re a local takeout spot. Can we leave a few menus by your register for customers who ask about food?"

A small worked example: say you print 500 flyers and place them in 10 nearby spots, 50 per spot. If even a few households or coworkers keep one and order later, the flyer may be worth more than a broad ad that never reaches hungry people nearby. You do not need big numbers to make the point. Plug in your own print cost, your own distribution spots, and your own average order value.

For local marketing, pair flyers with your online listings and phone setup. A flyer can start the call. A good phone flow can finish it. If a caller asks about hours, parking, or allergens, ROAL can answer the routine questions and hand the tricky ones to staff with a summary. That keeps the flyer useful after it gets someone to pick up the phone.

sections.h2: How do I connect flyers to more phone orders?
sections.body:
The flyer should point people to one simple ordering path. For many restaurants, that path is the phone.

Try this structure:
- Top: food photo or strong headline
- Middle: 3 best-sellers and a short offer
- Bottom: phone number and a call-to-order line

Example call-to-order line: "Order by phone for pickup and delivery. We’ll confirm your items, ready time, and name."

If your restaurant gets a lot of calls during rush hours, a flyer can create demand at the same time your phones are already busy. That is where an [after-hours calls](/use-cases/after-hours) or [short-staffed shifts](/use-cases/short-staffed) setup can help. ROAL answers the phone, takes the order from the live menu, confirms it back, and sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen.

If you want a quick check on whether the phone is worth protecting, use this swap-in formula:
- Average order value: say $28
- Orders lost from missed calls: say 10 per week
- Weekly sales at risk: $280

Those are example numbers. Replace them with your own. The point is simple: a flyer can create the call, but the call has to be answered well.

If you want the flyer to feel more personal, add a handwritten-style note: "Ask for pickup specials when you call." That is short, specific, and easy to remember.

sections.h2: Should I print specials, coupons, or a full menu?
sections.body:
For most independent restaurants, a flyer should not try to do everything. The fuller the menu, the harder it is for a busy person to read.

Use this decision table:

| Flyer type | Best for | What to include |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Specials flyer | Quick repeat orders | 3-5 top items, one deal, phone number |
| Menu flyer | Takeout regulars | Best-sellers, combos, hours, address |
| Neighborhood flyer | Local awareness | Restaurant name, cuisine, map landmark, phone |
| Seasonal flyer | Limited-time push | Holiday items, catering note, ordering line |

If you run catering, a flyer can mention it, but keep the main focus on takeout unless you are specifically advertising events. If your goal is holiday trays or office lunches, link the flyer to a clear call to action and route those calls to staff when they need special handling.

One practical test: give the flyer to a friend who has never ordered from you. If they cannot tell what to order, when you are open, and how to call within 10 seconds, trim it down.

For more phone order ideas, see [rush-hour phone orders](/use-cases/rush-hour) and [menu, hours and allergen questions](/use-cases/menu-questions). Flyers work better when the rest of the phone flow is ready for the interest they create.

sections.h2: How can I use flyers without wasting money?
sections.body:
The easiest way to waste money is printing a flyer with no clear route to a call or repeat order. Before you print, make sure the menu, hours, phone number, and ordering path are correct.

A practical pre-print checklist:
- Phone number is large and easy to read
- Hours are current
- The top items are actually available
- No sold-out item is listed
- Address and neighborhood are correct
- The call-to-order message is short

If you need a simple phone setup, ROAL can be built from your website, Google Maps link, or restaurant name and city at /try. It reads public menu pages and menu files, then builds a phone host in about a minute. You can test-call it in the browser before going live.

You can also think about the cost side. Delivery apps commonly take roughly 15-30% commission per order. Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call. ROAL charges $0.90 per completed phone order, with no monthly fee, no setup fee, no per-minute fee, and no contract. Calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free.

That does not mean flyers should replace everything else. It means a flyer can be a low-friction way to get a nearby customer to call you directly instead of using a third party. If you want to try a simple setup, [build a free test host](/try).

takeaways: Restaurant flyers still work when they are short, local, and tied to a phone order.
List only the top items, current hours, and a large phone number.
Hand flyers out where nearby customers already live and work.
Use the flyer to drive calls, then make sure those calls are answered well.

faq.q: What should a restaurant flyer include?
faq.a: A good restaurant flyer should include your restaurant name, a few best-selling items, hours, address or neighborhood, and a large phone number. Keep the message simple so a customer knows what to order and how to reach you. If the flyer has too much text, it usually gets ignored.

faq.q: Do flyers work better than social posts for local takeout?
faq.a: They can, especially for nearby customers who already live or work close by. A flyer stays visible on a fridge, desk, or counter, while a social post can disappear quickly. Flyers are strongest when they push one clear action: call to order.

faq.q: Should I put my full menu on a flyer?
faq.a: Usually no. A flyer works better with a short list of your top items, a special, or a combo deal. If you print too much, people stop reading before they get to the phone number.

faq.q: How do I use flyers to get more pickup orders?
faq.a: Put the phone number in a large font and add a short line like, "Call to order pickup from our live menu." Hand the flyer out in nearby neighborhoods, apartment buildings, offices, and shops. Then make sure your phone system can answer quickly and take the order cleanly when people call.
